interpretation_correction.supersedes: frontier-s5-stabilizer-census-20261116.json stated stabilizer order is the leading structural predictor of family-internal redundancy, based on remaining-subset measurements (18/10/3/5 children)
interpretation_correction.correction: the P family (identity-only stabilizer) shows 36.68% full-family duplication across 116 children - nearly the class4 (38.0%) and audit_blocked (37.75%) levels. Family-internal duplication is driven primarily by FAMILY SIZE (cumulative union overlap over many children); stabilizer order is a secondary modifier. Q (order-4, 33 children) at 41.41% sits above the size trend, and the identity-family P at 116 children shows the lowest rate, so the stabilizer effect is real but modest
interpretation_correction.prior_data_validity: the census data itself remains correct; only the causal reading of the 1.4-2.75% trivial-family values was confounded by their tiny remaining subsets (3 and 5 children)
interpretation_correction.practical_consequence: family-level orbit transfer should be applied to ALL families (not only the 8 nontrivial-stabilizer ones) - expected remaining-subset savings scale with subset size and structure; a global cross-family table adds only ~1% (full families) to ~0.1% (frontier-top remaining) on top

recommendation.p_sweep: when the P engine sweep runs (24 remaining children / cost 1704), apply family-level orbit-level verdict transfer like Q: family-internal duplication is high (36.68% full-family; remaining-24 subset will be lower but structurally similar to class4's remaining measurement)
recommendation.table_priority: implement per-family seen-orbit tables first; the global table is a second-order refinement at the current frontier

interpretation_guard.no_verdict_claim: this measurement contains no win/loss verdicts and changes the status of no root
interpretation_guard.full_family_vs_remaining: full-family dup rates (36-41%) describe complete families; engines only search remaining subsets whose dup rates are lower
interpretation_guard.cross_family_scope: the 65f/63a census overlap (8.95% re-search redundancy) concerned two specific paired sweeps sharing folded roots; the frontier-top families measured here show much smaller cross-family overlap
